title: Tight guarantee for online knapsack (unit-density / IID): is it (1-e^{-2})/2?
short_statement: In online knapsack, items must be irrevocably accepted or rejected. For the unit-density (reward = size) and IID special cases, the best known guarantee relative to the fluid benchmark is $\approx 0.355$ and no policy beats $\approx 0.432$. The conjecture is that the tight guarantee equals $(1 - e^{-2})/2 \approx 0.432$.
open_problem: Determine the tight competitive ratio for unit-density online stochastic knapsack; in particular, prove or refute the conjectured value $(1-e^{-2})/2$.
background: Unit-density stochastic knapsack has reward equal to item size. Its standard ex-ante capacity LP is a stronger benchmark than expected offline packing, so constants relative to these benchmarks cannot be interchanged.
full_statement: A capacity-one knapsack faces independent requests $S_t\in[0,1]$ from known, possibly heterogeneous distributions in a fixed order. On observing $S_t$, a policy accepts or rejects it irrevocably, keeping total accepted size at most one. Reward equals accepted size. Define the standard ex-ante relaxation $$UP=\sup_{0\le x_t(s)\le1}\left\{\sum_t\mathbb E[S_t x_t(S_t)]:\sum_t\mathbb E[S_t x_t(S_t)]\le1\right\}.$$ For positive UP, determine the largest universal ratio of expected online reward to UP. The reviewed lower and upper bounds are $0.3557$ and $(1-e^{-2})/2$. This is not the ratio to the expected offline integral optimum.
known_results: Jiang, Ma, and Zhang, arXiv:2107.02058v4, Section 5.2, give the $0.3557$ unit-density guarantee relative to the standard ex-ante LP. Proposition 3 bounds that LP-relative guarantee by $(1-e^{-2})/2$. Their Section 2.5 explicitly distinguishes a $1/2$ guarantee against offline packing for a single knapsack. Thus the quoted smaller constants concern LP rounding, not an IID-only model or the offline benchmark. The broader arbitrary reward/size model has the separate tight LP-relative constant $1/(3+e^{-2})$.

progress.summary: Benchmark and heterogeneous-arrival scope corrected. The reviewed source leaves the LP-relative interval unmatched.

links.title: Jiang, Ma, Zhang, multi-unit prophet and online stochastic knapsack

counterexample_rationale: Upper-bound instances are finite stochastic knapsack instances and can be searched, but proving a tight upper bound for all policies is harder than finding examples.
alphaevolve_rationale: Automated search can optimize threshold/best-fit policies, discover potential invariants, and search for hard instances. The objective and benchmark are computable for discretized instances.

literature.synthesis: The stronger LP benchmark permits reductions to multiple resources; replacing it with the offline packing optimum changes the question and invalidates the stated upper-bound comparison.

reviewed.ref: Jiashuo Jiang, Will Ma, Jiawei Zhang, 'Tight Guarantees for Multi-unit Prophet Inequalities and Online Stochastic Knapsack', SODA 2022
reviewed.result: Section 5.2 and Proposition 3 give the unit-density LP-relative bounds; Section 2.5 distinguishes the offline benchmark.

reviewed.ref: Clifford Stein, Van-Anh Truong, Xinshang Wang, 'Advance Service Reservations with Heterogeneous Customers', Management Science 2020
reviewed.result: Studies a stochastic resource-allocation/appointment-scheduling model and obtains the earlier $0.321$-type guarantee for the unit-density setting.

reviewed.ref: Saeed Alaei, 'Bayesian Combinatorial Auctions: Expanding Single Buyer Mechanisms to Many Buyers', FOCS 2011
reviewed.result: Introduces influential multi-unit prophet-inequality techniques used as benchmarks for online allocation and stochastic knapsack.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Promising directions include improving the utilization invariant in Jiang-Ma-Zhang, designing policies that adapt more sharply to residual capacity, or solving factor-revealing programs for small discretized instances to infer a tight policy. For upper bounds, search for capacity profiles where all online policies either fill too early or leave too much slack.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: Use the explicit LP in the formal statement and fixed-order independent requests. Do not transfer offline-relative, IID-only, or simultaneous-multiple-resource results without a reduction.

where_posed.text: Posed in Will Ma's Online Resource Allocation course notes, Remarks 7.3-7.4, and suggested again by Will Ma as a problem close to his research.
